sif_reason: The incident involved exposure to a 440 V, 400 A electrical panel during energization. A phase-to-ground/phase-to-panel fault produced an electrical arc flash that reached the operator. An arc flash at this voltage/current level could result in fatal burns, electrocution, or other life-threatening injuries.
evidence_text: The operator removed the lock, opened the 440 V/400 A electrical board, and lifted the thermomagnetic breaker. This caused phase-to-ground/phase-to-panel contact and an arc flash, which reached and injured the operator.
hazard_notes: Electrical energy / arc flash while operating an energized 440 V, 400 A electrical installation.
consequence_notes: Fatality or life-altering injury, including severe thermal burns, electric shock/electrocution, cardiac arrest, or secondary injuries.
barrier_notes: Failed/inadequate electrical isolation and energization controls. The lock was removed and the panel was opened before energization, exposing the operator to hazardous electrical energy. Controls such as verified de-energization, lockout/tagout, absence-of-voltage testing, appropriate panel protection, and arc-flash PPE appear to have been ineffective or not followed.

description: The employee reports that he was draining ammonia, used as a refrigerant, into a container of water when splashes of the solution drained onto his face.
normalized_description: the employee reports that he was draining ammonia used as a refrigerant into a container of water when splashes of the solution drained onto his face
sif_reason: Ammonia is a highly corrosive, toxic, and volatile chemical. As a refrigerant-grade substance, it is typically concentrated, and its reaction with water can be exothermic, generating heat and caustic splash. Facial exposure carries elevated risk of severe chemical burns, eye damage (including permanent vision loss), and respiratory injury from inhaling ammonia vapor/fumes released during the draining process. Even without a stated severe outcome, the combination of hazard energy (concentrated ammonia), exposure route (facial splash), and proximity to eyes/airway meets the threshold for SIF-potential classification.
evidence_text: "draining ammonia, used as a refrigerant, into a container of water when splashes of the solution drained onto his face"
hazard_notes: corrosive/toxic substance (ammonia refrigerant), with potential exothermic reaction when combined with water, plus inhalation hazard from vapor release
consequence_notes: Under a worse-case variation (higher ammonia concentration, larger splash volume, direct eye contact, or prolonged inhalation), this could result in permanent eye injury/blindness, severe chemical burns to the face, or respiratory tract damage — clearly meeting SIF severity criteria
barrier_notes: Weak/failed — no indication of face shield, chemical splash goggles, or respiratory protection being used during the draining task; also suggests inadequate procedure/engineering controls (e.g., no closed-system transfer, no fume extraction, no controlled-rate draining) for handling a hazardous refrigerant chemical
exposure_notes: Direct facial splash contact with the ammonia-water solution during a manual draining/decanting task; likely concurrent inhalation exposure to ammonia fumes given proximity to the face
